chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Be callers to goodness for the people without your tongues, so that they may see from you striving, truthfulness, and piety.
ai.seo_question: How can Muslims invite others to goodness without speaking?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the concept of da'wah by emphasizing silent, embodied witness over verbal proclamation, a principle central to Shia emphasis on the integrity of the Imams and the faithful. By manifesting ijtihad, sidq, and wara', believers become living proofs of faith, aligning with the Shia scholarly tradition that views practical piety as the most potent form of invitation. This hadith underscores that true leadership in community is established through moral consistency rather than rhetorical skill.
